4642.summary: Army's $22B IVAS contract transferred from Microsoft to Anduril (Feb 2025), Army signed contract novation Apr 10, 2025. Anduril assumes production oversight, hardware/software development, delivery timelines. Microsoft remains 'preferred hyperscale cloud provider.' By Sep 2025, Army awards SBMC (IVAS Next) contracts: $159M to Anduril and $195M to startup Rivet for 18-month rapid prototyping. Total Anduril DoD contract value in USASpending: $169M+ across 20 awards including $94M for Altius 600M-V loitering munitions production.
4642.detail: IVAS timeline: (1) 2021: Microsoft wins $21.9B 10-year production contract. (2) 2022: DoD Inspector General warns Army could be 'wasting $22B if soldiers don't like IVAS.' Soldiers report discomfort, dizziness, nausea, reliability issues. (3) 2023: Multiple delays, Congressional funding blocks. (4) Jan 2025: Army issues IVAS Next RFI, kickstarts possible recompete. (5) Feb 11, 2025: Microsoft-Anduril partnership announced, Anduril to take over. (6) Mar 2025: IVAS Next renamed Soldier Borne Mission Command (SBMC), full and open competition announced. (7) Apr 10, 2025: Army signs contract novation, formally transferring Microsoft's contract terms to Anduril. (8) Sep 2025: SBMC contracts awarded to Anduril ($159M) and Rivet ($195M). Army FY2025 budget requested $255M to procure 3,162 IVAS 1.2 HUDs plus $58.6M in RDT&E.

evidence.evidence_ref: Breaking Defense 2025/02, 2025/04, 2025/09; Microsoft press release 2025/02/11; Congress.gov CRS IF13022; CNBC 2025/02/11; USASpending.gov

4679.summary: IVAS contract novation deep dive: Microsoft won original 10-year, $22B contract in 2021 for 120,000+ custom HoloLens headsets. After years of delays and performance issues, Microsoft discontinued HoloLens production in 2024. Feb 11, 2025: Microsoft and Anduril announced partnership/transfer. Apr 10, 2025: Army signed formal contract novation. Palmer Luckey described transfer as 'employees, hardware, IP, facilities, everything.' Tom Keane (Anduril SVP Engineering, former Microsoft Azure executive who came with the transfer) reported software release cycle reduced from 180 days to 18 hours. Sep 2025: Army awarded SBMC (IVAS Next) contracts — $159M to Anduril, $195M to startup Rivet for 18-month rapid prototyping.
4679.detail:
Timeline:
2018-19: Army prototyping contracts to Microsoft for HoloLens-based mixed reality headsets
March 2021: Microsoft wins $21.88B IVAS production contract (10-year IDIQ, 120,000+ headsets)
2021-2024: Repeated testing failures, soldier complaints (nausea, field of view too narrow), Congress restricts funding
Late 2024: Microsoft discontinues HoloLens consumer/enterprise product line
Feb 11, 2025: Microsoft and Anduril announce expanded partnership. Anduril to assume oversight of production, hardware/software development, delivery timelines, hiring decisions.
Apr 10, 2025: Army formally approves contract novation — slides Microsoft's contract terms entirely to Anduril.
Sep 2025: Army awards SBMC (IVAS Next) contracts: $159M to Anduril, $195M to Rivet for 18-month rapid prototyping.

Key personnel: Tom Keane, Anduril SVP of Engineering — former Microsoft Azure executive who transitioned with the contract. He led the technical transfer.

Microsoft retains role as 'preferred hyperscale cloud provider' for Azure workloads related to IVAS and Anduril AI.

Software improvements: Keane highlighted release cycle improvement from 180 days to 18 hours (developer to warfighter).

Critical question: How did a company founded in 2017 take over a $22B contract from Microsoft? The answer appears to be: (1) Microsoft failed to deliver; (2) Anduril's Lattice platform provided a ready software foundation; (3) Tom Keane personally bridged the organizations; (4) Political alignment — Anduril is the preferred defense tech vendor of the current administration.

evidence.evidence_ref: Breaking Defense Feb 2025, CNBC Feb 2025, Breaking Defense Apr 2025, Microsoft press release Feb 2025, CRS IF13022

4719.summary: Operation Epic Fury confirmed as first large-scale AI-coordinated military operation. Palantir's AIP platform used for intelligence fusion, target identification, and battlefield simulation via partnership with Anthropic (Claude AI) and AWS. Anduril's Lattice software managed autonomous drone swarms alongside LUCAS kamikaze drones (SpektreWorks). Shield AI's Hivemind piloted autonomous CCA platforms. Task Force Scorpion Strike operated LUCAS + Lattice-networked drone swarms. Palantir stock rose 5.8% on Mar 2. Claude AI reportedly used for intelligence assessment and strike planning hours AFTER Trump signed ban on Anthropic — DoW ignored the ban.
4719.detail: The Iran conflict validates and operationalizes the entire defense tech capture structure: (1) Palantir provides data fusion and targeting — the AI 'brain' of strike planning; (2) Anduril provides autonomous hardware (drone swarms via Lattice, potentially Fury CCA in theater) and software coordination; (3) SpaceX/Starshield provides satellite communications for autonomous systems including LUCAS drones; (4) D-Wave's quantum optimization (10x speedup in missile defense planning) is exactly what is needed for the real-time threat assessment happening now. The Hegseth-Anthropic confrontation reveals the military's growing dependence on AI — when Amodei refused to remove guardrails, the Pentagon used Claude anyway through existing Palantir integrations.

evidence.evidence_ref: NPR 2026-03-01, Democracy Now 2026-03-03, Reuters/Al-Monitor 2026-03-03, Futurism 2026-03-01, Interesting Engineering 2026
